key_insight: The U-statistic structure of GRPO policy gradients turns group-size selection from trial and error into a variance-ratio estimation problem.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive group sizing can reduce policy-gradient error and improve reasoning-model training over fixed group sizes with modest additional computational cost.
method: Express GRPO group-size selection through policy-gradient variance components.
Use a pessimistic ratio estimator that accounts for denominator uncertainty.
Apply a jackknife-based selection rule and characterize three sample-size regimes.
evidence_signal: Experiments on synthetic Reasoning Gym tasks and real-world mathematical reasoning and code-generation benchmarks report lower policy-gradient mean squared error and improved policy optimization.
watch_item: Near-zero variance-ratio denominators make estimation difficult, so uncertainty handling is crucial for reliable group-size selection.
